details:
Project Details – Project: Space Mission

Our project, Project: Space Mission, is an interactive educational space mission game developed using TurboWarp and Piskel. The game allows players to independently carry out space missions to collect scientific data from destinations such as the Moon and Mars. Players must manage their spacecraft, maintain sufficient energy supplies, overcome unexpected obstacles, and make important decisions to successfully complete their missions.

The project provides several educational benefits by introducing children and students, especially those interested in STEM, to the challenges of space exploration. Through gameplay, players can develop essential skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making, resource management, resilience, and perseverance. The intended impact is to increase young learners' curiosity about space exploration and encourage them to pursue an interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

To develop the game, we used TurboWarp to program the game's systems, mechanics, and interactive features. We also used Piskel to create pixel-art sprites, characters, spacecraft designs, and animations. These tools allowed us to combine coding and digital art to create an engaging gaming experience.

The creativity of our project comes from transforming the complex process of planning and carrying out a space mission into an interactive game that is enjoyable and educational. Instead of simply learning about space missions through textbooks, players can experience simulated challenges and understand the consequences of their decisions.

Throughout development, our team considered several important factors, including gameplay accessibility, educational value, mission objectives, spacecraft maintenance, limited energy supplies, unexpected constraints, and resource management. We also considered how to make the game engaging and understandable for younger audiences while ensuring that its challenges encourage players to think critically and make strategic decisions.

Ultimately, Project: Space Mission aims to make space exploration more accessible, enjoyable, and educational, inspiring the next generation of young learners to explore STEM and develop skills that can be applied beyond the game.

How to play:

1. In Phase 1, the start of the game, the player must open the computer and select the mission and neccesary spacecraft parts to build the rocket. After chosing and exitting the computer, the player must click the button with an arrow to continue to Phase 2.

2. In Phase 2, the player must manage the rocket and themselves while travelling to the moon. For example, the player has to open the radar (The red button in the first room of Phase 2) and steer the spacecraft from the asteroid, and try to manage everything within the time. The time for Phase 2 is based on the mass of the spacecraft, the bigger the mass, the longer it takes to finish.

3. Once the timer reaches zero, go to the "Control Room" and click "Send Rover" to see the player's results and win.
